title: SF1262 (2017-2018 Regular): Gun violence protective orders authorization

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/90/2017/0/SF/1262/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Version read: introduced (as filed). No passage vote recorded. Includes an emergency order (245.9904), return of firearms (245.9906), liability protection (245.9908), and a filing offence. Section 9 adds clause 14 to the ineligible-persons list in 624.713 and strikes a period in clause 13.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 245.9901, subd. 4): (a) There shall exist an action known as a petition for a gun violence protective order for protection from gun violence, which order shall enjoin and prohibit the respondent from possessing firearms for a fixed period. (b) A petition for relief under sections 245.9901 to 245.9908 may be made by any family or household members, by the chief law enforcement officer or a designee, a city or county attorney, or by a guardian as defined in section 524.1-201, clause (26).
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 245.9902, subd. 2): (d) If the court finds there is a preponderance of the evidence to issue a gun violence protective order, the court shall issue the order prohibiting the person from possessing a firearm for the duration of the order. (e) The order shall have a fixed period, to be determined by the court, of not less than six months and not more than two years, subject to renewal or extension under section 245.9903.
Section 5 (Minn. Stat. 245.9905): (a) Upon issuance of a gun violence protective order, the court shall direct the respondent to transfer any firearms the person possesses, within 24 hours, to a federally licensed firearms dealer, a law enforcement agency, or third party.
Section 7 (Minn. Stat. 245.9907, subd. 2): A person who possesses a firearm and knows or should have known that the person is prohibited from doing so by a gun violence protective order under section 245.9902 or 245.9904, or by an order of protection granted by a judge or referee pursuant to a substantially similar law of another state, is guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be prohibited from possessing firearms for a period of five years.
Section 9 (Minn. Stat. 624.713, subd. 1): (14) a person who is subject to a gun violence protective order as described in section 245.9902 or 245.9904.
